Localizing AI, for me, is not a slogan. It is a question: where does this AI really work, and for whom?
A small model, trained on satellite data around Kairouan, works in central Tunisia and in Morocco, and fails in the Sahel.
So an AI is not global. It has a climate, a language, a phone, and people.
That is why our method is simple.
We start from free global data. We check it against local reality: Tunisian weather stations, and farmers' own rain reports.
We write the test before we run it. We train one small model per climate.
We publish what fails. And a technician always stays in the loop.
